=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- agents.md:1997-2000 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The paragraph now claims "every failback target keeps a 1M+ token window because reviewer prompts regularly exceed 250K tokens," but the live-roster mapping includes `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro -> deepseek/deepseek-v3.2` and `minimax/minimax-m3 -> minimax/minimax-m2.5`. The catalog shows `deepseek/deepseek-v3.2` at `context_window: 128000` and `minimax/minimax-m2.5` at `context_window: 200000` (both well below 1M). A reviewer prompt that exceeds 200K would silently overflow those slots rather than fit comfortably.
  WHY: Operators reading the agents.md paragraph are told every failback target can absorb the >250K-token reviewer prompt. When the failback fires for a deepseek/minimax slot, the prompt gets truncated and the review produces low-quality findings, but nothing in the runtime signals that the fallback is undersized — the slot "succeeds" at producing a (truncated, low-quality) review. The previous wording limited the 1M+ claim to "the three new failback targets for Gemini, Grok, and GLM," which is the only set actually true. The PR generalized that sentence when it dropped Grok from the default roster.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:4114-4120 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `case "${wd_reason}" in max_steps|tool_repeat) … esac` override at lines 4114-4120 is unreachable in the current code path: every kill path in the watchdog that writes `max_steps` or `tool_repeat` to `${wd_reason_file}` immediately calls `exit 145`/`exit 146`, which terminates the script before control returns to the post-wait section. `wd_reason` is written nowhere else. The override is therefore dead defensive code that will never fire.
  WHY: Not a runtime defect today, but it documents a misleading invariant ("a loop-guard kill must never be read as a clean exit") that the existing control flow actually prevents, and the comment risks future maintainers trusting the safety net and removing the explicit `exit` codes from the kill paths. Leaving it in place is fine; the comment should at least note that the override exists for an unreachable branch so the kill-path `exit` is not deleted as redundant.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:3991 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: If the watchdog polls during the small window before `codex_pid_file` is written, `cpid` is empty and `_reviewer_kill_pid ""` is invoked. The function's empty-pid handling is not visible in the diff; if it does not short-circuit on empty input, the loop-guard kill silently no-ops while the child keeps running, and the parent shell remains parked in `wait` until `HEARTBEAT_MAX_WALL` fires (defeating the loop guard).
  WHY: Same race already exists for the pre-existing `idle_timeout` / `max_wall` paths, so this is consistent with the script's existing behavior; the new code adds two more paths that inherit the same latent bug. A one-line defensive `[ -n "${cpid}" ] || continue` before `_reviewer_kill_pid` would close it for both kill paths.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- agents.md:2000 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The text over-generalizes from the old accurate claim ("the three new failback targets for Gemini, Grok, and GLM keep 1M+ token windows") to "every failback target," which is factually wrong. `deepseek/deepseek-v3.2` has `context_window: 128000` (scripts/codex_model_catalog.json:267) and `minimax/minimax-m2.5` has `context_window: 200000` (scripts/codex_model_catalog.json:27). Both are below 1M and below the 250K prompt threshold the text cites as the reason for the claim. An operator relying on this statement would assume all failback targets can handle 250K+ token reviewer prompts, when two cannot.
  WHY: No runtime code impact, but the documentation is factually incorrect and could mislead operators sizing prompt budgets or investigating failback failures. The prior text was accurate; this PR's diff introduced the error by broadening "the three new failback targets" to "every failback target."
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
